title: GeoPark, Colombian Civil Air Patrol complete 21 medical brigades after third visit to Puerto Lopez
summary: In the most recent brigade, 7 out of 10 people who attended were women, 65.1% live in rural areas of the municipality, 29% were under 18 years old, 4% belong to indigenous communities and 0.5% to the Afro-descendant population.
body_markdown:
**Since 2017, more than 12,000 people from Casanare and Meta have benefited from medical brigades that have brought specialized and free services to communities with higher barriers to accessing healthcare.**


GeoPark and the Colombian Civil Air Patrol (PAC) have worked together for over nine years to provide free of charge specialized medical services to the most vulnerable communities in the regions where the Company operates. Through this partnership, 21 medical brigades have been held between 2017 and 2025, benefiting 12,206 people, mainly in populations that face difficulties in accessing specialized care.


The partnership held its 21


st


Medical Brigade on November 6-7, the third in Puerto Lopez. At the Enrique Olaya Herrera Educational Institution, around 619 people accessed health services and benefited from 700 specialized consultations in optometry, pediatrics, dermatology, gynecology, and urology, as well as breast and prostate cancer screenings, diagnostic ultrasounds, and family planning procedures.


In the most recent brigade, 7 out of 10 people who attended were women, 65.1% live in rural areas of the municipality, 29% were under 18 years old, 4% belong to indigenous communities and 0.5% to the Afro-descendant population.


“This partnership demonstrates the value of pooling capacities and maintaining sustained work with specialized organizations to meet our neighbors’ needs. For nine years we have brought health services closer to communities facing barriers to access, turning our commitment to Good Neighborliness into concrete actions that contribute to their well-being and health,” GeoPark Nature and Neighbors Director Anibal Fernandez de Soto said.


“Returning to Puerto Lopez gives us the opportunity to continue the work we have built together with GeoPark to bring specialized medical services to those who most need them. This new brigade underscores our commitment to putting the experience of our health professionals and volunteers at the service of families in Puerto Lopez who require specialized care,” Colombian Civil Air Patrol General Director Pamela Estrada said.


The brigade was made possible thanks to the coordination between the Colombian Civil Air Patrol, Puerto Lopez City Hall, Puerto Lopez Local Hospital, and GeoPark.


Through the medical brigades, GeoPark continues to strengthen a long-term partnership that contributes to the well-being of communities, under its commitment to Create Value and Give Back and the principle of Good Neighborliness that guides its relationships with territories.


**ABOUT GEOPARK**


GeoPark (NYSE: GPRK) is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company with more than 20 years of operations across Latin America and a proven track record in value creation. Its two-pillar strategy aims to maximize its core platform in Colombia, where it is one of the main operators, and to build a new long-term growth engine in Vaca Muerta – one of the world’s largest unconventional fields – and Venezuela through starting to operate the Bare block.
